investigation.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Cluster Nodes
investigation.summary: All three remote-agent checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in the production-api environment because every pod submitted for remote agent creation was left unschedulable: the 2 nodes carrying the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource reported insufficient capacity, and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity or selector. No evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was collected because agent creation never progressed past the scheduling phase.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents feature has exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm resource on the 2 nodes that carry it. With 0/6 nodes available and preemption unable to help, every new remote-agent pod is stuck in Pending/Unschedulable state. Because the agent pod never starts, the eval runner's createAgent call (infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs line 1885) never returns a VM ID or a ready state, so all four required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) remain absent and the expected-output contract defined in infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json lines 254-259 cannot be satisfied. This is an eval-observed infrastructure capacity constraint; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.
proof: failed-check.message: '0/6 nodes are available: 2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector. preemption: 0/6 nodes are available: 2 No preemption victims found for incoming pod, 4 Preemption is not helpful for scheduling.' — pod was unschedulable for 132s before the check timed out.

failed-check.timing: status=fail latencyMs=135103 — the check ran for ~135s, well within the outageLatencyMs threshold of 360000ms, confirming the failure is a hard scheduling block rather than a latency regression.
failed-check.evidence: empty object {} — zero evidence fields were written, consistent with the runner never reaching the post-scheduling code path in infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs.

expected-output.missing-required-evidence: all four required fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) are absent, matching the contract defined at infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json lines 256-259.
sibling.remote-agent-state: identical scheduler message ('2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm'), pod stuck for 147s — confirms the capacity exhaustion is not isolated to a single probe invocation.
sibling.remote-agent-runtime: identical scheduler message, pod stuck for 142s — third independent confirmation of the same node-level constraint.

source-context.infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs:1877-1885: runner calls createAgent(args, track, 'remote', null, orgId) at line 1885; if the resulting pod never schedules, no evidence can be written and the check fails with the scheduler message.

source-context.infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json:250-258: contract requires vmIdPresent===true and remoteState oneOf ['running','idle','ready']; neither assertion can be evaluated when evidence is empty.
possibleCauses: Primary — kata.peerpods.io/vm resource exhaustion on the 2 eligible nodes: all available VM slots are occupied by existing agents or leaked pods, leaving no capacity for new scheduling requests. Supported directly by failed-check.message, sibling.remote-agent-state, and sibling.remote-agent-runtime.

Secondary — node affinity/selector mismatch on the remaining 4 nodes: those nodes are not labeled or tainted to accept remote-agent pods, so even if VM capacity were freed, only the 2 kata-capable nodes could ever schedule these pods. This structural constraint amplifies any capacity pressure.

Tertiary — pod or VM resource leak: previously created remote-agent pods (possibly from earlier eval runs or user sessions) may not have been cleaned up, holding kata.peerpods.io/vm slots. The withCleanup wrapper in run-status-probes.mjs is designed to handle this, but a prior failed cleanup could leave orphaned pods consuming capacity.

Lower confidence — transient cluster event (node restart, maintenance drain): one or both kata-capable nodes may have been temporarily cordoned or drained, reducing effective VM capacity to zero at the time of the run. No node-event evidence is present in the packet to confirm or deny this.

investigation.title: Remote Agents: All Three Checks Failing Due to Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity on Kubernetes Cluster
investigation.summary: All three remote-agents checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in the production-api environment because every pod submitted by the eval runner was rejected by the Kubernetes scheduler with an Unschedulable verdict: the two nodes carrying the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource had no remaining capacity, and the four remaining nodes did not satisfy the pod's node affinity or selector requirements. Because no pod was ever scheduled, the agent was never created, and the eval runner could not collect any of the four required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, readyState, state), causing a complete contract gap.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the production-api remote-agent runtime has exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm resource on the two eligible nodes. The scheduler message "0/6 nodes are available: 2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector" (evidence: failed-check.message, sibling.remote-agent-create, sibling.remote-agent-runtime) is identical across all three sibling checks, confirming the failure originates at the VM scheduling layer before any agent lifecycle logic executes. This is an infrastructure capacity constraint, not an application code defect. No user-traffic or incident signals are present in the packet, so impact is scoped to this observability eval run.

sibling.remote-agent-runtime: identical Unschedulable root cause, pod stuck for 142s, zero evidence collected.

source-context.infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json:258-266: remote-agent-state contract requires readyState and state, which are only reachable after a pod is running.
possibleCauses: Primary — kata.peerpods.io/vm resource exhaustion on the two affinity-eligible nodes: concurrent workloads or a previous eval run left VM slots occupied, leaving zero capacity for new probe pods. Supported by all three sibling check messages reporting the same scheduler verdict.

Secondary — node affinity or node selector misconfiguration: the pod spec targets only 2 of 6 nodes via affinity/selector, artificially constraining the schedulable pool. If those two nodes are healthy but simply full, this is a capacity issue; if the selector is overly restrictive, it may be a configuration issue. The scheduler message distinguishes both conditions simultaneously.

Tertiary — cluster under-provisioning: the total number of kata.peerpods.io/vm slots across the cluster may be insufficient to absorb concurrent eval runs plus production workloads, indicating a need for additional node capacity or resource quota tuning.
Lower confidence — transient spike: a burst of remote agent creation requests from other sources may have temporarily exhausted VM slots; slots may self-recover once those agents are deleted.

investigation.summary: All three remote-agent eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api on 2026-06-27 with identical Kubernetes scheduling errors reporting that 0/6 nodes could schedule the requested pod: 2 nodes had insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity and 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. Because the pod never became schedulable, the agent was never created, and the runtime eval produced zero evidence — all 5 required fields (orgId, agentId, model, provider, message) are missing. This is an eval-detected infrastructure capacity failure localized to the remote-agent VM scheduling layer; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing remote agent provisioning in production-api has exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm resource quota on the 2 nodes that match the remote-agent pod's node affinity/selector. With 0 schedulable nodes and preemption unable to free capacity, every attempt to create a remote-agent pod times out unscheduled (~132–155 s across all three checks). The eval runner calls createAgent(..., "remote", ...) in run-status-probes.mjs (line 1918), which depends on a schedulable VM-backed pod; because that pod never starts, no agent identity or runtime response is ever returned, causing the complete absence of all required evidence fields defined in check-expectations.json (lines 266–270).

possibleCauses: [Most likely] kata.peerpods.io/vm resource quota exhausted on the 2 affinity-matching nodes: the scheduler message explicitly states 'Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm' on those nodes, and preemption found no victims to evict, indicating all VM slots are occupied by existing pods.

[Likely contributing] Node affinity/selector mismatch on the remaining 4 nodes: those nodes are structurally ineligible for remote-agent pods regardless of capacity, reducing the effective scheduling pool to only 2 nodes and making the cluster more sensitive to VM slot exhaustion.

[Possible] A surge in concurrent remote-agent pod requests (e.g., from other eval runs, user workloads, or a leaked/un-cleaned pod from a prior eval run) consumed all available kata.peerpods.io/vm slots before this eval's pods could be scheduled.

[Low probability] A misconfiguration in the pod's resource request for kata.peerpods.io/vm (requesting more slots than any single node can provide) could cause permanent unschedulability, but this would be a regression requiring a config change not evidenced in the supplied suspect changes.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Cluster Nodes
investigations.summary: All three remote-agent checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in the production-api environment because every pod submitted for remote agent creation was left unschedulable: the 2 nodes carrying the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource reported insufficient capacity, and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity or selector. No evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was collected because agent creation never progressed past the scheduling phase.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents feature has exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm resource on the 2 nodes that carry it. With 0/6 nodes available and preemption unable to help, every new remote-agent pod is stuck in Pending/Unschedulable state. Because the agent pod never starts, the eval runner's createAgent call (infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs line 1885) never returns a VM ID or a ready state, so all four required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) remain absent and the expected-output contract defined in infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json lines 254-259 cannot be satisfied. This is an eval-observed infrastructure capacity constraint; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.
proof: failed-check.message: '0/6 nodes are available: 2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector. preemption: 0/6 nodes are available: 2 No preemption victims found for incoming pod, 4 Preemption is not helpful for scheduling.' — pod was unschedulable for 132s before the check timed out.

failed-check.timing: status=fail latencyMs=135103 — the check ran for ~135s, well within the outageLatencyMs threshold of 360000ms, confirming the failure is a hard scheduling block rather than a latency regression.
failed-check.evidence: empty object {} — zero evidence fields were written, consistent with the runner never reaching the post-scheduling code path in infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs.

expected-output.missing-required-evidence: all four required fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) are absent, matching the contract defined at infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json lines 256-259.
sibling.remote-agent-state: identical scheduler message ('2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm'), pod stuck for 147s — confirms the capacity exhaustion is not isolated to a single probe invocation.
sibling.remote-agent-runtime: identical scheduler message, pod stuck for 142s — third independent confirmation of the same node-level constraint.

source-context.infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs:1877-1885: runner calls createAgent(args, track, 'remote', null, orgId) at line 1885; if the resulting pod never schedules, no evidence can be written and the check fails with the scheduler message.

source-context.infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json:250-258: contract requires vmIdPresent===true and remoteState oneOf ['running','idle','ready']; neither assertion can be evaluated when evidence is empty.
possibleCauses: Primary — kata.peerpods.io/vm resource exhaustion on the 2 eligible nodes: all available VM slots are occupied by existing agents or leaked pods, leaving no capacity for new scheduling requests. Supported directly by failed-check.message, sibling.remote-agent-state, and sibling.remote-agent-runtime.

Secondary — node affinity/selector mismatch on the remaining 4 nodes: those nodes are not labeled or tainted to accept remote-agent pods, so even if VM capacity were freed, only the 2 kata-capable nodes could ever schedule these pods. This structural constraint amplifies any capacity pressure.

Tertiary — pod or VM resource leak: previously created remote-agent pods (possibly from earlier eval runs or user sessions) may not have been cleaned up, holding kata.peerpods.io/vm slots. The withCleanup wrapper in run-status-probes.mjs is designed to handle this, but a prior failed cleanup could leave orphaned pods consuming capacity.

Lower confidence — transient cluster event (node restart, maintenance drain): one or both kata-capable nodes may have been temporarily cordoned or drained, reducing effective VM capacity to zero at the time of the run. No node-event evidence is present in the packet to confirm or deny this.

whatWouldDisproveThis: If kubectl describe node on the 2 kata-capable nodes shows available kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity greater than zero at the time of the eval run, resource exhaustion is not the cause and a different scheduling constraint (e.g., a quota, admission webhook, or pod disruption budget) must be investigated.
If the pod scheduling error message changes on re-run to a different failure reason (e.g., image pull error, OOM, or API auth failure), the root cause is not VM capacity exhaustion.

If a re-run of the eval immediately after the failure succeeds and produces all four required evidence fields, the failure was transient (e.g., a brief node drain or a race with another pod being deleted) rather than a sustained capacity exhaustion.

If only remote-agent-create fails on re-run while remote-agent-state and remote-agent-runtime pass, the failure is isolated to the create path rather than a shared infrastructure constraint, weakening the capacity-exhaustion hypothesis.

If no pods holding kata.peerpods.io/vm resources are found in the cluster namespace, the resource exhaustion hypothesis is weakened and a node label/taint misconfiguration or quota enforcement becomes the more likely cause.
followUpEvals: Add a dedicated eval that probes kata.peerpods.io/vm allocatable vs. requested capacity across all cluster nodes and warns before exhaustion reaches 100%, providing earlier signal than waiting for a pod to fail scheduling.

Add a node-affinity coverage eval that verifies the number of nodes matching the remote-agent pod selector meets a minimum threshold (e.g., at least 2 schedulable nodes with available VM slots), alerting on structural scheduling risk before a live failure.

Add a stale-pod cleanup eval that detects remote-agent pods older than a configurable TTL in the cluster namespace, catching resource leaks from failed withCleanup executions before they exhaust VM capacity.

Consider adding a pre-flight scheduling dry-run check (e.g., using kubectl --dry-run=server) as an early gate in the remote-agent-create probe so that scheduling failures are detected and reported with richer context before the full pod creation timeout is reached.

investigations.title: Remote Agents: All Three Checks Failing Due to Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity on Kubernetes Cluster
investigations.summary: All three remote-agents checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in the production-api environment because every pod submitted by the eval runner was rejected by the Kubernetes scheduler with an Unschedulable verdict: the two nodes carrying the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource had no remaining capacity, and the four remaining nodes did not satisfy the pod's node affinity or selector requirements. Because no pod was ever scheduled, the agent was never created, and the eval runner could not collect any of the four required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, readyState, state), causing a complete contract gap.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the production-api remote-agent runtime has exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm resource on the two eligible nodes. The scheduler message "0/6 nodes are available: 2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector" (evidence: failed-check.message, sibling.remote-agent-create, sibling.remote-agent-runtime) is identical across all three sibling checks, confirming the failure originates at the VM scheduling layer before any agent lifecycle logic executes. This is an infrastructure capacity constraint, not an application code defect. No user-traffic or incident signals are present in the packet, so impact is scoped to this observability eval run.
proof: failed-check.message: scheduler reports '2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm' and '4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector' for the remote-agent-state pod, which was stuck unscheduled for 147s.
failed-check.timing: latencyMs=155452, well above the warningLatencyMs=240000 threshold is not yet breached, but the pod never reached a running state before the eval timed out.
sibling.remote-agent-create: identical Unschedulable root cause, pod stuck for 132s, zero evidence collected.
sibling.remote-agent-runtime: identical Unschedulable root cause, pod stuck for 142s, zero evidence collected.
expected-output.missing-required-evidence: all four required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, readyState, state) are absent because the agent pod never started.

source-context.infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json:258-266: remote-agent-state contract requires readyState and state, which are only reachable after a pod is running.
possibleCauses: Primary — kata.peerpods.io/vm resource exhaustion on the two affinity-eligible nodes: concurrent workloads or a previous eval run left VM slots occupied, leaving zero capacity for new probe pods. Supported by all three sibling check messages reporting the same scheduler verdict.

Secondary — node affinity or node selector misconfiguration: the pod spec targets only 2 of 6 nodes via affinity/selector, artificially constraining the schedulable pool. If those two nodes are healthy but simply full, this is a capacity issue; if the selector is overly restrictive, it may be a configuration issue. The scheduler message distinguishes both conditions simultaneously.

Tertiary — cluster under-provisioning: the total number of kata.peerpods.io/vm slots across the cluster may be insufficient to absorb concurrent eval runs plus production workloads, indicating a need for additional node capacity or resource quota tuning.
Lower confidence — transient spike: a burst of remote agent creation requests from other sources may have temporarily exhausted VM slots; slots may self-recover once those agents are deleted.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 3 Remote-Agent Checks
investigations.summary: All three remote-agent eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api on 2026-06-27 with identical Kubernetes scheduling errors reporting that 0/6 nodes could schedule the requested pod: 2 nodes had insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity and 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. Because the pod never became schedulable, the agent was never created, and the runtime eval produced zero evidence — all 5 required fields (orgId, agentId, model, provider, message) are missing. This is an eval-detected infrastructure capacity failure localized to the remote-agent VM scheduling layer; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing remote agent provisioning in production-api has exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm resource quota on the 2 nodes that match the remote-agent pod's node affinity/selector. With 0 schedulable nodes and preemption unable to free capacity, every attempt to create a remote-agent pod times out unscheduled (~132–155 s across all three checks). The eval runner calls createAgent(..., "remote", ...) in run-status-probes.mjs (line 1918), which depends on a schedulable VM-backed pod; because that pod never starts, no agent identity or runtime response is ever returned, causing the complete absence of all required evidence fields defined in check-expectations.json (lines 266–270).

source-context.infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs:1910-1918: runner calls createAgent(args, track, 'remote', null, orgId) at line 1918, confirming the eval requires a live schedulable remote pod.

source-context.infra/evals/status/features.json:181-189: all three remote-agent checks are registered under the same feature (remote-agents), explaining why a single scheduling failure cascades to all three checks.
possibleCauses: [Most likely] kata.peerpods.io/vm resource quota exhausted on the 2 affinity-matching nodes: the scheduler message explicitly states 'Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm' on those nodes, and preemption found no victims to evict, indicating all VM slots are occupied by existing pods.

[Likely contributing] Node affinity/selector mismatch on the remaining 4 nodes: those nodes are structurally ineligible for remote-agent pods regardless of capacity, reducing the effective scheduling pool to only 2 nodes and making the cluster more sensitive to VM slot exhaustion.

[Possible] A surge in concurrent remote-agent pod requests (e.g., from other eval runs, user workloads, or a leaked/un-cleaned pod from a prior eval run) consumed all available kata.peerpods.io/vm slots before this eval's pods could be scheduled.
[Possible] A node or VM-pool scaling event (scale-in, node failure, or maintenance) reduced available kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity below the minimum needed to schedule new remote-agent pods.

[Low probability] A misconfiguration in the pod's resource request for kata.peerpods.io/vm (requesting more slots than any single node can provide) could cause permanent unschedulability, but this would be a regression requiring a config change not evidenced in the supplied suspect changes.

recommendedNextActions: Immediately check kata.peerpods.io/vm slot availability on the 2 affinity-eligible nodes in the production cluster. If all slots are consumed, identify which pods hold them and whether any can be safely evicted or cleaned up.

Audit the production namespace for leaked or stuck remote-agent pods from prior eval runs. The eval runner uses withCleanup (run-status-probes.mjs line 1916), but interrupted runs may have bypassed cleanup, accumulating idle pods that hold VM slots.

If VM slot exhaustion is confirmed, evaluate whether the kata.peerpods.io/vm quota on the eligible nodes needs to be increased, or whether additional affinity-eligible nodes should be added to the cluster to provide scheduling headroom for concurrent eval and user workloads.

Review the node affinity/selector configuration for remote-agent pods to determine whether the 4 currently ineligible nodes could be made eligible, expanding the scheduling pool and reducing sensitivity to per-node VM slot exhaustion.

Monitor the remote-agents feature health status: with remote-agent-create and remote-agent-state both failing (both required=true) and outageAfterFailures=2 (infra/evals/status/features.json line 188), the feature has met the outage threshold in the eval system. Confirm whether this aligns with any operational status page or alerting policy.

After restoring scheduling capacity, re-run all three remote-agent checks to confirm recovery and verify that the runtime eval produces all 5 required evidence fields and that the message assertion ('hello from aura') passes.

recommendedVerifierProbes.reason: Confirms that the 4 nodes excluded by affinity are intentionally ineligible and that the 2 eligible nodes are the correct scheduling targets, ruling out an affinity misconfiguration as the primary cause.

whatWouldDisproveThis: If the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource on the 2 affinity-eligible nodes shows available (unallocated) slots at the time of the failure, the exhaustion hypothesis would be weakened and a different scheduling or admission cause should be investigated.

If the pod spec's kata.peerpods.io/vm resource request quantity exceeds the per-node maximum allocatable amount, the failure would be a permanent misconfiguration rather than a capacity exhaustion event.

If a re-run of the eval immediately after the failure succeeds and the pod schedules without any cluster changes, the failure was transient (e.g., a briefly occupied slot freed up) rather than a sustained capacity shortage.

If only remote-agent-runtime failed while remote-agent-create and remote-agent-state passed in the same run window, the failure would be isolated to the runtime probe rather than a shared scheduling bottleneck — but the evidence shows all three failed.

If the 4 nodes excluded by affinity/selector were actually eligible (i.e., the affinity config changed to include them), the effective scheduling pool would be larger and the capacity exhaustion framing would need revision.
followUpEvals: Add a pre-flight eval that checks kata.peerpods.io/vm allocatable vs. requested capacity on affinity-eligible nodes before attempting remote-agent pod creation, surfacing capacity exhaustion as a distinct check rather than a scheduling timeout.

Add a leaked-pod detection eval that counts running or pending remote-agent pods in the production namespace and alerts if the count exceeds the expected maximum for a single eval run, catching cleanup failures before they exhaust VM slots.

Add a node-affinity coverage eval that verifies at least N nodes match the remote-agent pod's affinity/selector and have non-zero kata.peerpods.io/vm availability, providing early warning when the eligible node pool shrinks.

Consider a synthetic scheduling dry-run eval (using a pod with the same resource requests but no actual workload) that can detect scheduling failures faster than the full agent-creation timeout, reducing the latency before an alert fires.
